commits.message:
fix(box): declare each box style as the reference's own 8x4 grid (rich-table-6uy.3) (#94)

* fix(box): declare each box style as the reference's own 8x4 grid (rich-table-6uy.3)

A `BoxChars` carried five of the reference's eight grid lines. The three it
dropped are the row separator, the footer separator and the footer content row,
so a table with `showLines` or a footer drew the head-to-body glyphs where Rich
draws `├───┼───┤`, and no data edit could have fixed it — the type had nowhere
to put them.

Seven of the nineteen constants were also wrong on fields that did exist:
ASCII's top and bottom dividers, and the whole MINIMAL and SIMPLE families.

Both defects have one cause. The eighteen named fields were a second,
differently-shaped map of a territory the reference publishes as an 8x4
character grid, and every constant was a hand transcription into that shape —
including a name collision that inverts a box if read literally, since the
field named `mid` held the reference's line 3 while the reference's own `mid_*`
is line 4. So the fix is to stop transcribing: a `Box` is now built from the
grid itself, which can be diffed against `rich/box.py` character for character,
and the row glyphs are reachable only by what a row *is* (`getRow`,
`getContentChars`) rather than by a name that can be matched to the wrong line.

The nineteen constants were generated from the reference, not retyped. Frames
verified by rendering every one of them as a table with a header, two body rows,
row separators and a footer, and diffing all nine lines against expectations
computed from `rich/box.py`: 19/19 match, and corrupting one grid line makes the
diff red on exactly that row.

`Table` needed no edit — the level already crossed as a value, which is the seam
.1 and .2 left open for this. `Panel` reads `box.top`/`box.bottom` as records now
and takes its body verticals from `getContentChars("row")`.

The grid also carries `mid` as the reference means it: a blank spacer holding the
body verticals, not a rule.

611 lines to 435, while tripling the data each constant carries.

* fix(box): require a grid row to draw four cells, not merely count four

The constructor checked that a row held four characters. That is half the
invariant: a grid column is one drawn glyph position and a table's widths are
measured in terminal cells, so "🌟─┬┐" passed the count and silently drew a
five-cell row, breaking the frame of every table using that box — far from the
line that caused it.

Both legs are now required and both are pinned by a test that fails when either
is removed: four characters, because getEdge indexes the four positions, and
four cells, because that is what is drawn. The previous test claimed to prove
the character count was not a UTF-16 count and could not — its input was all
BMP, so both readings agreed and reverting the check left it green.

* docs(test): stop the sentinel-grid comment overclaiming

It said all thirty-two characters were distinct and that swapping any two
would turn the test red. Thirty are distinct; a content row's fill column is a
space in three of them, and swapping two never-drawn characters cannot fail
anything. The claim that survives is about drawn positions.

* docs(box): stop the mid arm citing an option this port lacks

The comment justified the spacer row by Table's `leading`, which exists in the
reference and in docs/tables.md but not in src/ (rich-table-jx1). The reference
is the reason the row has this shape; say that instead.
